record.title: Dankelmann–Laskar's simultaneous domination conjecture for two graphs
record.statement:
Let $\gamma_{\rm sd}(2,2,n)$ denote the maximum, over pairs of graphs of order $n$, of the minimum size of a set that simultaneously dominates both graphs. **Dankelmann–Laskar's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma_{\rm sd}(2,2,n)=3n/5.
$$

The conjecture concerns the sharp value of the simultaneous domination parameter for two graphs. The preceding theorem establishes the lower bound $\gamma_{\rm sd}(2,2,n)\geq 3n/5$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is always attained as an upper bound as well.
record.source_name: Yair Caro and Michael A. Henning, “Simultaneous Domination in Graphs”, arXiv:1301.4008 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.4008

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Nef effectiveness conjecture for surfaces over finite fields
record.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over $\bar{\mathbb F}_p$, and let $L$ be a nef line bundle on $X$. The **Iitaka dimension** $\kappa(L)$ is the maximum dimension of the images of the rational maps defined by positive tensor powers of $L$. **Nef effectiveness conjecture.** One has $\kappa(L)\geq 0$; equivalently, there is a positive integer $m$ such that $L^{\otimes m}$ has a nonzero section. If $L^2>0$, then $\kappa(L)=2$, so the unresolved case may be assumed to have $L^2=0$.
record.source_name: Adrian Langer, “On positivity and semistability of vector bundles in finite and mixed characteristics”, arXiv:1301.4450 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.4450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Sarwate's minimum-distance conjecture for binary cyclic codes
record.statement:
Let $m=2t$, let ${\mathbb F}$ be the finite field of size $2^m$, and let ${\mathcal C}_d$ be the binary cyclic code of length $2^m-1$ and dimension $2m$ with two nonzeros ${\alpha}^{-1}$ and ${\alpha}^{-d}$, where $\alpha$ is a primitive element of ${\mathbb F}$ and $\gcd(d,2^m-1)=1$. The **Sarwate conjecture.** The minimum distance of ${\mathcal C}_d$ is at most

$$
2^{m-1}-2^t.
$$

This conjecture concerns the minimum distance, equivalently the Walsh spectrum, of binary cyclic codes with two primitive nonzeros. It is attributed to Dilip V. Sarwate and is described in the source as a challenging well-known conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Tao Feng, Ka Hin Leung and Qing Xiang, “Binary Cyclic codes with two primitive nonzeros”, arXiv:1301.4773 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.4773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: DeMarco–Kahn conjecture for sparse random Turán identities
record.statement:
Let $t\geq2$ be an integer, let $G(n,p)$ be the binomial random graph, let $\operatorname{ex}_G(K_{t+1})$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $K_{t+1}$-free subgraph of $G$, and let $\operatorname{col}_G(t)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $t$-colorable subgraph. **DeMarco–Kahn conjecture.** There exists $C>0$ such that, whenever

$$
p\geq C\left(\frac{(\log n)^{1/(t-1)}}{n}\right)^{2/(t+2)},
$$

we have asymptotically almost surely

$$
\operatorname{ex}_G(K_{t+1})=\operatorname{col}_G(t).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by requiring that every edge lie in sufficiently many copies of $K_{t+1}$; the source does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Vojtěch Rödl and Mathias Schacht, “Extremal results in random graphs”, arXiv:1302.2248 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2248

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Lombardi's stronger conjecture on derived invariance of canonical cohomology
record.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth projective varieties over the complex numbers, let $\mathbf{D}(X)=\mathbf{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{Coh}(X))$ and $\mathbf{D}(Y)=\mathbf{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{Coh}(Y))$, and let $F$ denote the induced correspondence on the relevant pairs consisting of an identity functor and a line bundle parameter. For each $i$, let $V^i(\omega_X)_0$ and $V^i(\omega_Y)_0$ be the unions of the irreducible components through the origin of the corresponding cohomological support loci. **Lombardi's stronger conjecture.** Assume that $\mathbf{D}(X)\simeq\mathbf{D}(Y)$. Then

$$
F(\operatorname{id}_X,V^i(\omega_X)_0)=(\operatorname{id}_Y,V^i(\omega_Y)_0)
$$

for all $i$, and if $\alpha\in V^i(\omega_X)_0$ and $F(\operatorname{id}_X,\alpha)=(\operatorname{id}_Y,\beta)$, then

$$
h^i(X,\omega_X\otimes\alpha)=h^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes\beta).
$$

The claim is intended to imply both the cohomological-support-locus conjecture and the special Hodge-number conjecture. The source notes that a more general statement involving dimensions of cohomology groups was proved for $i=0,1$, while the general form remains open.
record.source_name: Luigi Lombardi and Mihnea Popa, “Derived equivalence and non-vanishing loci II”, arXiv:1302.2259 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Defect bound by equivalent matrices conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a complex Hadamard matrix, let $d(H)$ denote its defect, and let $|1\in\widetilde{H}|$ be the number of entries equal to $1$ in a matrix $\widetilde{H}$. Two complex Hadamard matrices are equivalent when one is obtained from the other by the equivalence operations of Definition 1.3.

**Defect bound conjecture.** We have

$$
d(H)\leq\max|1\in\widetilde{H}|,
$$

where the maximum ranges over all matrices $\widetilde{H}$ equivalent to $H$.

The claim seeks to bound the deformation-theoretic defect using the largest possible number of unit entries among equivalent representatives. The source presents it as part of a broader attempt to recover the defect from the statistics of these unit-entry counts; its resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Teodor Banica, “First order deformations of the Fourier matrix”, arXiv:1302.4153 (2013).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0707.1852](https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1852).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4153

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2013). “Here is actually the simplest counterexample, with $w=e^{2\pi i/30}$: $$w^5+w^6+w^{12}+w^{18}+w^{24}+w^{25}=0$$ So, what Conjecture 1.8 says is that such a ``tricky sum'' cannot be used for constructing a complex Hadamard matrix.”

record.title: The bounded domination conjecture for transitive colorings
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament whose edges are colored transitively with $k$ colors; that is, each color class induces a transitive digraph. Write $dom(T)$ for the minimum size of a dominating vertex set.

**Bounded domination conjecture.** For each positive integer $k$ there is a least integer $p(k)$ such that every $k$-transitive tournament $T$ satisfies $dom(T)\le p(k)$.

The claim is immediate for $k=1,2$, since every $2$-transitive tournament is transitive. It is stated to remain open for $k\ge 3$; examples and results in the paper rule out certain potential counterexamples.
record.source_name: Dömötör Pálvölgyi and András Gyárfás, “Domination in transitive colorings of tournaments”, arXiv:1302.4677 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4677

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2013). “Conjecture is open for $k\ge 3$.”

record.title: Simple closed geodesics realizing the intersection-form constant on hyperbolic surfaces
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_s$ denote the moduli space of surfaces of constant negative curvature with genus $s$. For a surface $(M,g)$, let $K(M,g)$ be the maximum in Equation (def K) associated with the intersection form.

**Simple-geodesics realization conjecture.** For any $s>1$, for almost every $(M,g)$ in $\mathcal{M}_s$, $K(M,g)$ is realized by the homology classes of simple closed geodesics.

This conjecture concerns whether the extremal intersection-form constant on a generic constant-negative-curvature surface is attained by homology classes represented by simple closed geodesics. The source proposes it in analogy with a theorem of Thurston; its resolution is not established in the supplied context.
record.source_name: Daniel Massart and Bjoern Muetzel, “On the intersection form of surfaces”, arXiv:1302.4692 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4692

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Non-scaling conjecture for multi-hop interference networks with delayed CSI
record.statement: Let $K$ users communicate over a layered $M$-hop interference network with delayed channel-state information (CSI), and let its network sum-DoF be the supremum of achievable sum-DoFs. The condition $M=o(K)$ means that $M/K\to 0$ as $K\to\infty$. **Non-scaling conjecture.** The DoF of the $K$-user $M$-hop interference network with delayed CSI and $M=o(K)$ does not scale with $K$. The paper establishes DoF scaling for certain multi-hop networks, including networks with $2K$ or more hops, and identifies determining the minimum number of hops and relays per hop needed for scaling as an open problem; this conjecture proposes that sublinear hop count is insufficient.
record.source_name: Mohammad Javad Abdoli and A. Salman Avestimehr, “Layered Interference Networks with Delayed CSI: DoF Scaling with Distributed Transmitters”, arXiv:1302.4788 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4788

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2013). “Thus, the problem of characterizing the DoF scaling rate of this network with delayed CSI remains open.”

record.title: Falgas-Ravry–Vaughan conjecture for induced directed stars
record.statement:
Let $\vec{S}_k$ be the directed star on $k$ vertices, with one center and $k-1$ edges oriented away from it. For an integer $k\geq 3$, let $\pi_{\vec{S}_k}(\emptyset)$ denote the maximum induced density of $\vec{S}_k$ in a digraph. Define

$$
\alpha_k=\max_{0\leq x\leq 1}\frac{kx(1-x)^{k-1}}{1-x^k}.
$$

Assume the maximum is attained at $x=x_k$. **Falgas-Ravry–Vaughan's conjecture.**

$$
\pi_{\vec{S}_k}(\emptyset)=\alpha_k,
$$

and an extremal configuration is obtained by starting with parts $|A|=x_kn$ and $|B|=(1-x_k)n$, adding all edges oriented from $A$ to $B$, and iterating this construction inside $A$. The cases $k=3$ and $k=4$ are known by flag algebras, while the conjecture is open for general $k$, with computer-assisted methods becoming difficult as $k$ grows.
record.source_name: Hao Huang, “On the maximum induced density of directed stars and related problems”, arXiv:1303.3101 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.3101

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2013). “For example, the Tur\'an density of $K_4^{-}$ (the unique $3$-graph on $4$ vertices with $3$ edges) was conjectured to be achieved by the iterated blow-up of certain $6$-vertex $3$-graph by Frankl and Fur\"edi and is still open.”

record.title: Constant-congestion integrality-gap conjecture for maximum edge-disjoint paths in minor-closed families
record.statement: Let ${\cal G}$ be any proper minor-closed family of graphs. The **constant-congestion integrality-gap conjecture.** The integrality gap of the flow LP for maximum edge-disjoint paths is at most a constant $c_{\cal G}$ when congestion $2$ is allowed. This strengthens the question of whether all minor-closed graph families have a constant-factor constant-congestion integrality gap for maximum edge-disjoint paths; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Chandra Chekuri, Guyslain Naves and F. Bruce Shepherd, “Maximum Edge-Disjoint Paths in k-sums of Graphs”, arXiv:1303.4897 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4897

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2013). “The proof of Theorem and discussion of open problems are also moved to the appendix.”

record.title: Ideal-theoretic Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture for squarefree monomial ideals
record.statement: Let $I$ be a squarefree monomial ideal. A **minor** of $I$ is obtained by a sequence of quotients and localizations at variables, and the **monomial grade** of $I$ is the maximum length of a regular sequence of monomials in $I$. **Ideal-theoretic Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture.** If $I$ and all of its minors have equal height and monomial grade, then the associated graded ring $\operatorname{gr}_I$ is reduced; equivalently, $I$ is normally torsion-free. This is the complete algebraic reformulation given in the source of the packing-versus-max-flow-min-cut conjecture, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Christopher A. Francisco, Huy Tai Ha and Jeffrey Mermin, “Powers of squarefree monomial ideals and combinatorics”, arXiv:1303.6642 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.6642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: The largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue characterization of hyperstars
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be odd and let $G=(V,E)$ be a $k$-uniform connected hypergraph whose maximum degree is $d>0$. Let $\mathcal L$ be the Laplacian tensor of $G$.

**Hyperstar characterization conjecture.** The largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue $\lambda(\mathcal L)$ is equal to $d$ if and only if $G$ is a hyperstar.

For odd uniformity, the maximum degree is a tight lower bound for the largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue. The conjecture asserts that equality occurs exactly for hyperstars; the supplied text gives no evidence that this characterization has been resolved.
record.source_name: Shenglong Hu, Liqun Qi and Jinshan Xie, “The Largest Laplacian and Signless Laplacian H-Eigenvalues of a Uniform Hypergraph”, arXiv:1304.1315 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.1315

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Cox ring quotient conjecture for the del Pezzo fibration
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the projective bundle used to construct the threefold Mori dream space $X$, and let $f$ and $g$ be the defining equations of the two hypersurfaces whose complete intersection is $X$. **Cox ring quotient conjecture.** The Cox ring of $X$ is

$$
\operatorname{Cox}(X)=\dfrac{\operatorname{Cox}(\mathcal{F})}{(f,g)}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Cox ring of the complete-intersection Mori dream space is obtained by quotienting the Cox ring of its ambient projective bundle by the two defining equations. The supplied text gives no further evidence resolving the conjecture.
record.source_name: Hamid Abban, “On pliability of del Pezzo fibrations and Cox rings”, arXiv:1304.4357 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.4357

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: A basis conjecture for the Partition Temperley–Lieb algebra
record.statement:
Let ${\rm PTL}_n$ be the Partition Temperley–Lieb algebra, let $\mathsf{P}_n$ denote the set-partition monoid on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $F$ be a reduced word in the generators used for ${\rm PTL}_n$. **Basis conjecture.** The elements

$$
E_I F,\qquad I\in\mathsf{P}_n,
$$

form a linear basis of ${\rm PTL}_n$. Consequently,

$$
\dim({\rm PTL}_n)=b_n C_n.
$$

The conjecture concerns the spanning set constructed from the presentation of the Partition Temperley–Lieb algebra; proving linear independence would determine its dimension.
record.source_name: Jesús Juyumaya, “A Partition Temperley-Lieb Algebra”, arXiv:1304.5158 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Conjecture on the index of Chebyshev radical extensions
record.statement:
Let $\theta$ be a root of $\theta$'s defining polynomial 
$$
and let $
u_p$ denote the $p$-adic valuation. For an odd prime $p
eq\ell$ satisfying $t
gleich\pm2\pmod{p^2}$, define the $p$-index by
$$
. **Index conjecture.** If $p
eq\ell$ is an odd prime for which $t\equiv\pm2\pmod{p^2}$, then

$$
\nu_p(\operatorname{ind}(\Phi)):=\operatorname{ind}_p(\Phi)=\left\lfloor\frac{\nu_p(t^2-4)}{2}\right\rfloor\frac{\ell^n-1}{2}.
$$

This conjectural formula is intended to determine the contributions of odd primes $p\neq\ell$ to the index of the power basis in the Chebyshev radical extension. record.title: Li's conjecture on the complexity of generalized connectivity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $S$ be a $3$-subset of $V(G)$, and let $n=|V(G)|$. For a set $S$, write $ckappa(S)$ for the maximum number of internally disjoint trees connecting $S$.

**Li's conjecture.** Given $G$, $S$, and an integer $cell$ with $2\leq cell\leq n-2$, deciding whether

$$
ckappa(S)\geq cell
$$

is an $\mathcal{N}\mathcal{P}$-complete problem.

The conjecture concerns the unresolved case $k=3$ of the complexity of deciding whether a prescribed set can be connected by many internally disjoint trees. The corresponding problem is polynomial-time solvable when both $k$ and $cell$ are fixed, while it is known to be $\mathcal{N}\mathcal{P}$-complete for fixed $k\geq 4$; the $k=3$ case remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Lily Chen, Xueliang Li, Mengmeng Liu and Yaping Mao, “Further hardness results on the generalized connectivity of graphs”, arXiv:1304.6153 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6153

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Weak intersecting partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the set of all integer partitions of $n$, and let $P_n(1)$ be the set of partitions having $1$ as a part. Two partitions **intersect** if they have at least one common part, and a subset is intersecting if every two of its members intersect. **Weak Form.** $P_n(1)$ is an intersecting subset of $P_n$ of maximum size. This is the unrestricted-length version of the proposed Erdős–Ko–Rado-type principle for integer partitions; the source presents it as a conjecture without stating a resolution.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting integer partitions”, arXiv:1304.6563 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Strong intersecting partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $P_{n,k}$ be the set of partitions of $n$ of length $k$, and let $P_{n,k}(1)$ be the set of such partitions having $1$ as a part. Two partitions **intersect** if they have at least one common part, and a subset is intersecting if every two of its members intersect. **Strong Form.** For $2 \leq k \leq n$, $P_{n,k}(1)$ is an intersecting subset of $P_{n,k}$ of maximum size. This is the fixed-length refinement of the weak conjecture; the source later records partial results and cases where it is proved, but presents the general assertion as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting integer partitions”, arXiv:1304.6563 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: t-intersecting partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the set of all integer partitions of $n$. For partitions ${\bf a}$ and ${\bf b}$, say that they **$t$-intersect** if they have $t$ common parts, with multiplicities allowed, and let a subset be $t$-intersecting if every two of its members $t$-intersect. Define $P_n\langle t\rangle$ to be the set of partitions whose first $t$ entries are $1$. **The $t$-intersecting partition conjecture.** $P_n\langle t\rangle$ is a $t$-intersecting subset of $P_n$ of maximum size. The source introduces this as the unrestricted-length generalisation of the weak and strong forms and does not state a resolution of the general claim.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting integer partitions”, arXiv:1304.6563 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Fixed-length t-intersecting partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $P_{n,k}$ be the set of partitions of $n$ of length $k$, and let $P_{n,k}\langle t\rangle$ be the set of partitions whose first $t$ entries are $1$. Two partitions **$t$-intersect** if they have $t$ common parts, with multiplicities allowed, and a subset is $t$-intersecting if every two of its members $t$-intersect. **The fixed-length $t$-intersecting partition conjecture.** For $t+1 \leq k \leq n$, $P_{n,k}\langle t\rangle$ is a $t$-intersecting subset of $P_{n,k}$ of maximum size. The source proves substantial parameter ranges and discusses the boundary case $k=t+1$, but presents the assertion in general as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting integer partitions”, arXiv:1304.6563 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Properly t-intersecting partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the set of all integer partitions of $n$. Two partitions **$t$-intersect properly** if they have $t$ distinct common parts, and a subset is properly $t$-intersecting if every two of its members $t$-intersect properly. Let $P_n([t])$ denote the set of partitions containing each of $1,2,\ldots,t$ as a part. **The properly $t$-intersecting partition conjecture.** $P_n([t])$ is a properly $t$-intersecting subset of $P_n$ of maximum size. This is the distinct-common-parts analogue of the preceding conjectures; the source presents the unrestricted-length assertion without a resolution.
record.source_name: Peter Borg, “Intersecting integer partitions”, arXiv:1304.6563 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Perfect matching minimum degree conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $n$, $d$, and $k$ with $1\leq d\leq k-1$ and $n/k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m_d^{n/k}(k,n)$ denote the minimum integer $m$ such that every $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum $d$-degree at least $m$ has a perfect matching. **Perfect matching degree conjecture.** If $n$, $d$, $k$, and $n/k$ are integers, then

$$
m_d^{n/k}(k,n)= \left( \max\left\{\frac{1}{2}, 1-\left(\frac{k-1}{k}\right)^{k-d}\right\}+o(1)\right)\binom{n-d}{k-d}.
$$

This conjectured threshold concerns the minimum $d$-degree forcing a perfect matching and is known in several ranges, including $d\geq k-4$ and all cases with $k\leq 5$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn, Deryk Osthus and Timothy Townsend, “Fractional and integer matchings in uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1304.6901 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6901

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Non-realizability of $K_{3k+4}$ as a semi-arc $k$-visibility graph
record.statement:
Let $K_{3k+4}$ denote the complete graph on $3k+4$ vertices, and let a **semi-arc $k$-visibility graph** be a graph represented by semi-arcs with visibility determined by at most $k$ blockers. **Complete-graph non-realizability conjecture.** The complete graph $K_{3k+4}$ is not a semi-arc $k$-visibility graph.

This conjecture is presented as a consequence of the preceding maximum-edge conjecture: applying that bound at $n=3k+4$ would give fewer than the $\binom{3k+4}{2}$ edges of the complete graph. It remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Matthew Babbitt, J. T. Geneson and Tanya Khovanova, “On k-visibility graphs”, arXiv:1305.0505 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0505

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2013). “There are also similar open questions about arc $k$-visibility graphs.”

record.title: Strict exclusion conjecture for adjoining zero to positive sets
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$, let $B\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ be a set with $|B|=k-1$, and define $r_k:=\min\{|\Omega_2(A)|:|A|=k\}$, where

$$
\Omega_2(A)=\{\rho(M):M\in A^{2\times 2}\}.
$$

**Strict exclusion conjecture.** One has

$$
|\Omega_2(B\cup\{0\})|<r_k.
$$

This conjecture concerns whether sets containing zero can attain the minimum predicted by the preceding computational conjecture; its status is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: J. A. Dias da Silva and Pedro J. Freitas, “Counting Spectral Radii of Matrices with Positive Entries”, arXiv:1305.1139 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.1139

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Cranston–Rabern conjecture on maximum-degree cliques
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\Delta$ for its maximum degree, $\omega$ for its clique number, and $\chi$ for its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal{H}(G)$ be the subgraph induced by the vertices of degree $\Delta$. **Cranston–Rabern conjecture.** If $\chi\ge\Delta$, then

$$
\omega\ge\Delta\quad\text{or}\quad\omega(\mathcal{H}(G))\ge\Delta-4.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the paper’s main theorem by requiring a larger clique among the maximum-degree vertices. It is proved for $\Delta=6$ and $\Delta=7$, and for $\Delta=3k+1$ with $k\ge3$; the stated bound is expected to be tight because of the graph $O_5$.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Landon Rabern, “Graphs with χ=Δ have big cliques”, arXiv:1305.3526 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3526

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Pseudocenter conjecture for entropy on Mandelbrot wakes
record.statement:
Let $\theta_1<\theta_2$ be external angles whose parameter rays $R_M(\theta_1)$ and $R_M(\theta_2)$ land at the same parameter on the boundary of the Mandelbrot set. Let $h(\theta)$ be the entropy of the Hubbard tree corresponding to the parameter with external angle $\theta$, and let $\theta^*$ be the pseudocenter of the interval $[\theta_1,\theta_2]$. **Pseudocenter conjecture.** The maximum of the entropy on this interval is attained at its pseudocenter:

$$
\max_{\theta\in[\theta_1,\theta_2]}h(\theta)=h(\theta^*)
$$

This conjecture connects the combinatorial entropy of Hubbard trees with the geometry of wakes in the Mandelbrot set. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Giulio Tiozzo, “Topological entropy of quadratic polynomials and dimension of sections of the Mandelbrot set”, arXiv:1305.3542 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Half-class conjecture for non-nilpotent subsets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple group. For a non-trivial conjugacy class $C$ in $G$, let $\omega_\infty(C)$ denote the maximum size of a subset of $C$ that is non-nilpotent.

**Half-class conjecture.**

$$
\max\left\{\frac{\omega_\infty(C)}{|C|}\mid C\text{ is a non-trivial conjugacy class in }G\right\}\leq\frac12.
$$

The authors state that the bound is sharp: in $A_5$ and in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(7)$, certain conjugacy classes contain non-nilpotent subsets of half their size. The conjecture is presented as open in the supplied text and would imply that a simple group cannot contain a non-nilpotent conjugacy class.

record.title: Minimal-genus virtual Legendrian isotopy conjecture
record.statement: Let $F$ be a surface, and let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be Legendrian knots in $ST^*F$ that are isotopic as virtual Legendrian knots. Suppose that $F$ is the surface of smallest genus realizing knots in the virtual Legendrian isotopy class of $K_1$ and $K_2$. **Minimal-genus virtual Legendrian isotopy conjecture.** Possibly after a contactomorphism of $ST^*F$, the knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ are Legendrian isotopic in $ST^*F$. This is proposed as a Legendrian analogue of Kuperberg's minimal-genus result for virtual knots; the source does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Patricia Cahn and Asa Levi, “Vassiliev Invariants of Virtual Legendrian Knots”, arXiv:1305.5293 (2013).

record.title: Linear-query priority-queue algorithm for maximum st-flow in directed planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a directed planar graph with $n$ vertices and source $s$ and sink $t$. Consider an augmenting-path algorithm for computing a maximum $st$-flow in $G$.

**Priority-queue implementation conjecture.** Such an algorithm can be implemented with $O(n)$ queries to a priority queue.

This proposes extending the priority-queue implementation known for the $st$-planar case to directed planar graphs without requiring the source and sink to lie on a common face. The paper presents it as a promising direction for developing practical maximum-flow algorithms; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Derivative-chaos law conjecture for the maximum of log-correlated Gaussian fields
record.statement:
Let $(X_n)_n$ be a cutoff approximation of a centered Gaussian field on $[0,1]^d$ with logarithmic covariance, and set $c_n={\rm Var}(X_n)$. Let $M'$ be the derivative chaos and let $G_d$ be a random variable. **Derivative-chaos maximum conjecture.** As $n\to\widetilde\to
ginfty$, one has, in law,

$$
sup_{x in [0,1]^d} X_n(x)-\sqrt{2d}\,c_n+\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2d}}\ln c_n \to G_d,
$$

and there is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\mathds{E}[e^{-qG_d}]=\frac{1}{c^q}\Gamma\left(1+\frac{q}{\sqrt{2d}}\right)\mathds{E}\left[\left(M'([0,1]^d)\right)^{-\frac{q}{\sqrt{2d}}}\right].
$$
 The second-order maximum asymptotics are proved for the discrete Gaussian free field in dimension two, while the stated generality is presented as a conjecture by analogy with branching random walks.
record.source_name: Rémi Rhodes and Vincent Vargas, “Gaussian multiplicative chaos and applications: a review”, arXiv:1305.6221 (2013).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6221

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2013). “Several questions remain open about star scale invariance as mentioned in , inspired by the discrete multiplicative cascades case .”

record.title: The classification conjecture for hyperbolic doubly primitive knots in non-prime manifolds
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a **doubly primitive knot**, meaning a knot of the type specified by the paper's doubly primitive construction, in a non-prime $3$-manifold. Let $(p,q)$ be a surgery slope, and let $K_{r,s}^{p,q}$ denote the paper's knot associated to integers $r,s$.

**Doubly primitive knot classification conjecture.** If $K$ is hyperbolic, then

$$
K=K_{r,s}^{p,q}
$$

for some slope $(p,q)$ and integers $r,s\neq\pm1$.

The conjecture records the authors' failure to find other hyperbolic doubly primitive examples: attempts to generalize known sporadic constructions generally produced surgery duals of cabled knots or knots with Seifert-fibered exteriors. The claim is left as a direction for further investigation.
record.source_name: Kenneth L. Baker, “A Cabling Conjecture for Knots in Lens Spaces”, arXiv:1306.0596 (2013).

record.title: Anti-pencil conjecture for the maximum number of non-negative-sum subsets
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ real numbers with total sum zero, and let $\mu_k(A)$ denote the number of $k$-subsets of $A$ with non-negative sum. Let $\mu_{\max}(k,n)$ be the maximum of $\mu_k(A)$ over all such sets $A$.

**Anti-pencil conjecture.** If $n\geq 4k$, then

$$
\mu_{\max}(k,n)=\binom{n-1}{k}.
$$

The lower bound is attained by choosing exactly one negative element, yielding a $k$-anti-pencil. Determining $\mu_{\max}(k,n)$ is described as a wide open problem, and the conjecture asserts optimality of this construction in the stated range.
record.source_name: Tony Huynh, “Extremal Problems for Subset Divisors”, arXiv:1306.0943 (2014).
record.references:

record.title: Upper-bound conjecture for lines in rank-three matroids in \mathcal{U}(\ell)
record.statement:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{U}(\ell)$ denote the class of matroids with no $U_{2,\ell+2}$-minor. Let $M(q,q)$ be the rank-$3$ matroid used in the paper, and let $W_2(M)$ denote the number of rank-$2$ flats, or lines, of a matroid $M$.

**Rank-three line-count conjecture.** If $\ell$ is a sufficiently large integer and $M\in\mathcal{U}(\ell)$ has rank $3$, then

$$
W_2(M)\leq W_2(M(q,q))=q^2+\binom{q}{2}(q+1),
$$

where $q$ is the largest prime power such that $2q\leq\ell+2$.

This refines the failed Bonin bound for large $\ell$ by proposing the construction $M(q,q)$ as the extremal example. The source presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution of this stronger statement.

record.title: Patel's covering-fraction conjecture for three perfect matchings
record.statement:
For a cubic bridgeless graph $G$, let $m_t(G)$ be the maximum fraction of edges covered by $t$ perfect matchings, and let

$$
m_t=\inf_G m_t(G),
$$

where the infimum ranges over all cubic bridgeless graphs.

**Patel's conjecture.**

$$
m_3=\frac45.
$$

The value $m_2=\frac35$ is attained by the Petersen graph, and Patel conjectured that the corresponding extremal value for three perfect matchings is also attained there. The paper proves implications involving this bound but does not resolve the conjecture itself.

record.title: Bounded-oddness shortest cycle cover conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a snark, let $m$ be the number of edges of $G$, and let $o(G)$ denote its oddness. Write $scc(G)$ for the length of a shortest cycle cover. **Bounded-oddness conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that

$$
scc(G)\leq \frac{4}{3}m+c
$$

if $o(G)=2$. This proposes a constant additive error above the minimum possible cover length for snarks of oddness two; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Dispersive-shock and exponential blow-up-time conjecture for small-dispersion gKdV
record.statement:
Let $u_0\in L_2(\mathbb R)$ be smooth initial data with a single maximum, let $\epsilon\ll1$ be the dispersion parameter, and let $t_c$ be the break-up time of the corresponding generalized Hopf solution. **Small-dispersion gKdV conjecture.** For $n\geq4$, the solution of the gKdV equation has a dispersive shock for times between $t\sim t_c$ and the blow-up time $t^*$. Moreover,

$$
t^*(\epsilon)=t_0^*\exp(\alpha\epsilon),
$$

where $t_0^*>t_c$ and $\alpha$ are constant with respect to $\epsilon$. The claim summarizes the paper’s numerical findings for the dispersive shock and the dependence of blow-up time on small dispersion; it is presented as a conjectural analytic description rather than a theorem.
record.source_name: C. Klein and R. Peter, “Numerical study of blow-up in solutions to generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations”, arXiv:1307.0603 (2014).

record.title: Erdős–Gould–Yuster–P conjecture on monochromatic cycle partitions
record.statement:
The cycle partition number of an $r$-colored complete graph is the minimum number of vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles needed to cover all its vertices.

**Erdős–Gould–Yuster–P conjecture.** The cycle partition number of any $r$-colored complete graph is at most $r$.

The conjecture proposes a linear sharp-looking bound depending only on the number of colors, improving the previously stated quadratic-logarithmic upper bound. The source gives no resolution.

record.title: The polynomial-time threshold conjecture for minimum ℓ-degree perfect matching
record.statement:
Let $b4\in[0,1]$, let $k\geq 2$, and let $\ell\in[k-1]$. Define $\mathbf{PM}(k,\ell,\delta)$ to be the problem of deciding whether a $k$-graph on $n$ vertices with minimum $\ell$-degree at least $\delta\binom{n}{k-\ell}$ has a perfect matching. **The polynomial-time threshold conjecture.**

$$
\mathbf{PM}(k,\ell,\delta)\text{ is in P for }\delta>1-(1-1/k)^{k-\ell}.
$$

This is the algorithmic counterpart to the space-barrier threshold: the source notes NP-completeness below this threshold, while the asserted polynomial-time result remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Peter Keevash, Fiachra Knox and Richard Mycroft, “Polynomial-time perfect matchings in dense hypergraphs”, arXiv:1307.2608 (2014).

record.title: Minkowski-plane bead-gap tightness conjecture for Steiner minimum paths
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a set of $n$ terminals in a Minkowski plane $M$ with unit ball $B$, and let $T_S$ and $T_{\mathrm{opt}}$ be a $d_M$-SMT and a $d_M$-MSPT on $N$, respectively. **Minkowski-plane bead-gap conjecture.** The upper bound

$$
\mathrm{beads}(T_S)-\mathrm{beads}(T_{\mathrm{opt}})\leq 2n-4
$$

is tight if and only if $B$ is not a parallelogram. This conjecture concerns the sharp performance gap between Steiner minimum trees and minimum Steiner point trees in Minkowski planes; the supplied text gives no resolution.
